title: Flow Nozzle

introduction.definition: A flow nozzle is a differential-pressure flow element with a smoothly curved inlet and a cylindrical throat, installed between flanges. It is more rugged than an orifice plate, keeps its calibration at high velocities and temperatures, and has a lower permanent loss (ISO 5167-3).
applications: Gas flows at high Reynolds number
key_points: Higher cost than orifice, lower than venturi
Throat tap or corner taps per standard
introduction.summary: A flow nozzle is a differential-pressure flow element with a smooth, curved inlet leading to a cylindrical throat. It is more robust than an orifice plate and handles high-velocity, high-temperature and erosive flows such as boiler steam and feedwater, with a lower permanent loss than an orifice but higher than a venturi (ISO 5167-3).

working_principle.characteristic_curve: ΔP ∝ flow²; discharge coefficient C ≈ 0.98 – 0.99 at high Re.

pressure.title: Pressure profile
pressure.description: The smooth curved inlet accelerates the flow with little loss; pressure is lowest in the throat. Recovery downstream is limited (no diffuser), so permanent loss lies between an orifice and a venturi. Flow nozzles suit high-velocity steam and erosive flows (ISO 5167-3).

foundation: Support the meter run; avoid vibration at the transmitter.
alignment: Centre the element precisely in the pipe bore (eccentricity affects accuracy).
piping: Provide straight upstream/downstream lengths per ISO 5167 for the fittings present, or use a flow conditioner.
Slope impulse lines: liquids — transmitter below taps; gas — transmitter above taps.
commissioning: Fill/vent impulse lines; zero the transmitter with the equalising valve.
Check the flow computation (β, density, units).

video_tutorials.title: Flow Nozzle — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Flow Nozzle.
A flow nozzle is a differential-pressure flow element with a smoothly curved inlet and a cylindrical throat, installed between flanges.
It is more rugged than an orifice plate, keeps its calibration at high velocities and temperatures, and has a lower permanent loss (ISO 5167-3).
Typical applications include high-pressure steam and boiler feedwater; power-plant performance tests (ASME PTC 6); erosive or high-velocity flows; gas flows at high Reynolds number.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Carrier Flanges & Bolting.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Flow Nozzle works.
Flow enters the curved nozzle inlet smoothly.
Velocity is highest and pressure lowest in the throat.
The DP transmitter measures upstream and throat pressure.
Downstream the jet expands with partial pressure recovery.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
The smooth curved inlet accelerates the flow with little loss; pressure is lowest in the throat.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Flow Nozzle.
Check transmitter zero.
Inspect nozzle throat when line is open.
Replace gaskets; check nozzle alignment.
Watch for throat deposits: reading drift. Common cause: scaling (feedwater chemistry).
Watch for impulse line problems: erratic reading. Common cause: steam/condensate imbalance.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
